messages:
maya: FYI saw a 95p latency bump in ap-south dedicated pool at 02:14 UTC. GPUs steady but a handful of hosts show TX queue storms and packet drops.

trey: any tenant rollout or warmup around that time?

maya: tenant A ran a promo canary that triggered aggressive kvcache prefetches. logs show many short connections and simultaneous prefill waves from multiple allocs.

li: quick root-cause guess: aligned prefill fanout -> egress burst -> NIC queue saturation -> tx_dropped -> client retries. also saw SNAT mapping churn on the egress gateway.

maya: mitigation plan: 1) kinetic override to cap tenant A prefill_concurrency to 6 for 90m, 2) enable per-pool distributed SNAT routing to spread ephemeral port load, 3) scheduler scatter: add jitter to warmers so they don't align.

ops-bot: applying override for tenant A (prefill_concurrency=6 ttl=90m) (id ov-362a).

net-bot: routing change applied: ap-south/dedicated -> snat-33,snat-34 (id route-362b).

trey: immediate metrics: 95p down from 210ms -> 40ms in ~4m. good signal.

li: follow-ups: instrument per-tenant ephemeral port usage, alert at 60% of instance capacity; implement host-level tx_queue feedback that can throttle prefill rates dynamically.

maya: cost note: adding distributed SNAT config is low infra cost; dev work for scheduler + telemetry ~2 dev days.

ops-bot: incident tag `noisy-prefill-egress` created for postmortem.

maya: leaving canary at 10% and watching for 30m. ping if anything else pops up.
